table: Good conductors of heat and electricity
Mostly solids with high melting points

blocks.p: **Exceptions:** mercury is a liquid metal. Sodium and potassium are soft and can be cut with a knife. Gallium and caesium melt on the palm. Iodine is lustrous. Diamond (carbon) is the hardest natural substance. Graphite conducts electricity.

bullets: Metal + oxygen → **basic** oxide: 2Cu + O_{2} → 2CuO. Non-metal oxides are acidic or neutral.
**Amphoteric** oxides (Al_{2}O_{3}, ZnO) react with both acids and bases: Al_{2}O_{3} + 2NaOH → 2NaAlO_{2} + H_{2}O

With water: Na and K react violently with cold water: 2Na + 2H_{2}O → 2NaOH + H_{2} + heat. Ca reacts less violently. Mg reacts with hot water. Al, Fe and Zn react only with steam: 3Fe + 4H_{2}O → Fe_{3}O_{4} + 4H_{2}. Pb, Cu, Ag and Au do not react.
With dilute acids: metals above hydrogen give H_{2}. Nitric acid is an oxidising agent, so usually no H_{2} (except Mg and Mn with very dilute HNO_{3}).
Displacement: a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive one: Fe + CuSO_{4} → FeSO_{4} + Cu

box: **Reactivity series:**  K > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > Pb > [H] > Cu > Hg > Ag > Au

bullets: Formed by transfer of electrons. Na → Na^{+} + e^{–} and Cl + e^{–} → Cl^{–}
Hard solids with high melting and boiling points (strong forces between ions).
Soluble in water, insoluble in kerosene and petrol.
Conduct electricity when molten or in solution (ions can move), not when solid.

table: Roasting (sulphide) or calcination (carbonate), then reduction with carbon
2ZnS + 3O_{2} → 2ZnO + 2SO_{2};  ZnCO_{3} → ZnO + CO_{2};  ZnO + C → Zn + CO
Na at cathode, Cl_{2} at anode

blocks.p: **Thermite reaction:** Fe_{2}O_{3} + 2Al → 2Fe + Al_{2}O_{3} + heat (joins railway tracks). **Electrolytic refining:** impure metal is the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode, and impurities settle as anode mud.

bullets: Silver turns black (silver sulphide). Copper gets a green coat (basic copper carbonate). Iron rusts (needs both air and water).
Prevention: painting, oiling, greasing, galvanising (zinc coat), chrome plating, anodising, alloying.
Alloys: brass (Cu + Zn), bronze (Cu + Sn), solder (Pb + Sn, low melting point), stainless steel (Fe + Ni + Cr). 22 carat gold = 22 parts gold + 2 parts Cu or Ag.
